archetype: An aristocrats sacrifice engine that kills by drain. strategic_frame.json declares 'combo' and the artifacts agree: five tutors, six declared kill lines, fourteen checker-passed stacks. The 30 creatures read as an aggro count only because in this deck the fodder IS the combo. COUNTING CONVENTION, held on every axis below: every figure is deck-audit's, taken over all 100 copies, carried unrounded. Where the audit files a card's function under possible_uncounted (card-advantage, protection) the number is carried unchanged and the reading says what the oracle text shows.
verdict: The grind layer is genuinely well built: fodder and drain both at 82.3% drawn, outlets 78.5%, ignition 73.8%, turn-3 land drop 91.6%. The mana still functions after the reminder-text fix, but with a much thinner margin than the tracked diagnosis claimed — colour-sources is +2 over Karsten's target, not +5, which removes any land from the cut list and does NOT change what binds. What binds is unchanged: interaction-breadth at 2 of 5 classes, with artifact at zero by enumeration over all 80 entries, while this deck's own hosers (Grafdigger's Cage, Cursed Totem) are artifacts and three of six declared kills are commander-gated. The first table run adds one usable fact and one non-fact: the pod's clock is long (mean round 17.1, our seat eliminated at global turn 30.44), so the assisted assembly rates and not the by-turn-6 rates are the number that matters; and the 0.1 win rate is not a measurement, because Forge's own AI notes say it is 'pretty bad for most combo decks'.

engine.declared: Turn a renewable body into a death trigger, over and over, until stacked drains have taken the table's life total — Yawgmoth one free outlet among nine, with six declared kills on top: two Gravecrawler loops (A, B), the Exquisite Blood pair (C), the Mikaeus line (D), the Nest of Scarabs engine as primary (E, stacks 002/003/004), and the undying pair (F, stack 014, library-bounded).

components.reading: Nine drains, drawn 82.3% of games and 72.0% by turn 6. Tied with the fodder layer at 0.823 as the best-measured class in the deck, and all six declared kills name a drain component.

Nine renewable-fodder sources at 82.3%, 72.2% by turn 6. deck_recon.json (as_of 2026-08-03) named this as the archetype's load-bearing weakness and named Ophiomancer and Pawn of Ulamog as the fix; both are in the 99 and the component is no longer thin.

Eight free repeatable outlets not counting the commander, 78.5%. The deck mulligans to a class here, not to a card. Enumerated by type: five are creatures with activated abilities (Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Woe Strider, Yahenni, Warren Soultrader), three are artifacts (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Blasting Station).
Eight ways to place the first -1/-1 counter, 73.8%. Three double as the sweeper suite, so no sweeper slot is dead.
Five ways to turn a creature death into castable black, 61.2%. What makes a sacrifice loop mana-positive rather than merely free.

Fast mana. Of the seven targets the audit prices as a standalone class (sizes 9, 9, 8, 8, 5, 5, 3 at rates 0.823, 0.823, 0.785, 0.738, 0.612, 0.612, 0.436), this is both the smallest and the lowest-rated. It is where Culling the Weak is aimed. The audit's role-route closers (Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, Thought Vessel) are generic rocks and are not a recommendation here — deck_recon.json's mono-black finding prefers colour-specific rituals and cost reduction.
Five tutors, 61.2%. The reason every declared kill's assisted rate is a multiple of its unassisted one — KILL E goes 13.5% to 58.8%.

One card is the whole component, 17.1% unassisted and 67.0% with a tutor spent on it — a tutor spent on defence instead of a kill half. It answers a creature or an enchantment and cannot touch an artifact.

17.0%, the lowest measured rate of the three one-card components the audit prices on their own (Gravecrawler 0.17, Feed the Swarm 0.171, Bastion of Remembrance 0.178). Both unbounded kills (A, B) route through it.

Named in five of the fourteen checker-passed stack scenarios (002, 004, 009, 010, 011); by the same count Nest of Scarabs appears in twelve and Yawgmoth in nine. Redundant as a drain — there are nine — not as the specific drain those verified boards resolved with.

Read from oracle text, the in-format lookalikes do not substitute in this shell: Nether Traitor triggers only when ANOTHER creature dies, and Forsaken Miner returns on committing a crime, which sacrificing your own creature is not. single_points_of_failure.why: Three of the six declared kills (D, E, F) are commander-gated, including the primary. The gate is a timing tax rather than an access problem — he recasts from the command zone — but KILL E's 38.8% assisted by-turn-6 rate assumes he survives a rotation, and only three cards in the 99 can keep Yawgmoth on the battlefield through a removal spell or return him to it immediately: Lightning Greaves (shroud), Supernatural Stamina and Malakir Rebirth (return on death). Enumerated over every protection-shaped line in the 99, nothing else reaches him: Sedgemoor Witch's ward and Yahenni's indestructible are self-only, and Mikaeus grants undying to other NON-HUMAN creatures while Yawgmoth is a Human Cleric. Two of the three are invisible to the protection axis, which is why it reads 3 rather than 5.

cut_candidates.why: Four mana that does nothing on the turn it lands, in zero of the fourteen checker-passed stack scenarios and in none of the six declared kill lines, inside a removal count of 12 against a floor of 8. It is the slot the artifact answer has to come from: the mana axes leave no land available, and cutting from any engine component would trade a measured rate for a breadth class.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: It is the only removal:edict in the 99 and the only card that makes opponents sacrifice anything, so cutting it removes the deck's repeatable non-targeting removal ENGINE. What remains against a hexproof or ward board is the three sweepers (Black Sun's Zenith, Soul Snuffers, The Meathook Massacre), all one-shot, plus combat-dependent effects (Massacre Girl's wither, Ophiomancer's deathtouch Snake). With nine renewable fodder sources it triggers constantly, and the one table run points the other way from this cut: our seat was eliminated by damage in 9 of the 14 attributed eliminations, and giada-angels — the aggro seat Grave Pact taxes hardest — was the attributed killer 8 times. The two breakdowns are reported separately in the record and are not joined here. Interaction goes 12 to 11.

cut_candidates.why: Recursion is five by the taxonomy (Agadeem's Awakening, Persist, Phyrexian Reclamation, Reassembling Skeleton, Victimize) and functionally six, because Animate Dead does the same job while filed buff:attached / removal:debuff / value:etb. Victimize is in zero of the fourteen checker-passed stack scenarios, and at three mana sorcery speed it is the slowest member of that class.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: It is the CHEAPEST card in the 99 that returns two creature cards to the battlefield at once — the other multi-return is Agadeem's Awakening, which needs X to cover each returned card's mana value — and one of the routes that can put a legendary creature (Mikaeus, KILL D's piece, or Yawgmoth himself) from graveyard to battlefield; Persist reads 'nonlegendary', so the remaining legend routes are Animate Dead and Agadeem's Awakening at X>=4, the latter at seven or more mana. Its sacrifice cost is itself a death trigger for the drain layer. Recursion goes 5 to 4 by the taxonomy.

add_candidates.why: The artifact class is zero, re-enumerated over all 80 entries for this diagnosis, and this deck's hosers are artifacts: Grafdigger's Cage sits on both Gravecrawler loops and the undying returns, Cursed Totem on five of the eight outlets plus Yawgmoth. Gate converts the resource this deck has most of — a renewable body, drawn 82.3% of games — into artifact destruction every upkeep. Its roles are removal:spot, sac-cost, sac-outlet, so the breadth heuristic can see it and the interaction count holds at 12 when it replaces Grave Pact. open_questions.question: Under an opposing Grafdigger's Cage, do KILL A (stack 009), KILL B (011), KILL D (010) and KILL F (014) still function? A and B recast Gravecrawler from the graveyard; D and F return creature cards to the battlefield from the graveyard via undying.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If four of six declared kills die to one two-mana artifact the deck cannot remove, the Gate to Phyrexia add is undersold here rather than oversold, and it stops being a marginal breadth patch.

open_questions.question: Under an opposing Cursed Totem, what survives of the outlet component? Five of its eight members are creatures whose ability is activated (Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Woe Strider, Yahenni, Warren Soultrader) and Yawgmoth himself is shut off; three are artifacts (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Blasting Station).
open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the artifact-answer gap is only about graveyard hate or also collapses the outlet class the deck mulligans to.

open_questions.question: Does the corrected black-source count warrant a 37th land? The audit reads 38 sources against a target of 36; of the five nonland sources, Dark Ritual is one-shot and Pawn of Ulamog is credited only through mana_analysis's colour-identity fallback, since its sole mana clause is an Eldrazi Spawn token's 'Sacrifice this token: Add {C}'.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The deck is at 36 lands, the floor of the window, and turn-3 land drop is 91.6%. If the honest count is nearer 36 than 38 the margin is gone, and adding a one-shot ritual (Culling the Weak) does not restore it.

open_questions.question: How often does the deck assemble ANY of its six kills? The audit states its schema cannot express the union, and averaging the six would invent a number the simulation never measured.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The per-line rates (0.6% to 13.5% unassisted) understate the deck's real conversion, and the union is the number a pilot actually experiences at the table.

open_questions.question: Should the fast-mana any_of group be re-curated — adding Culling the Weak if it lands, and deciding whether Jet Medallion belongs, since it accelerates Yawgmoth to an effective three mana but is cost reduction rather than mana?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 43.6% figure is only as good as the declared group; a stale declaration leaves the next diagnosis prescribing against a number the deck has already moved.

open_questions.question: Is Withering Torment worth a third slot alongside Gate to Phyrexia? The two are named as closers for the same single point of failure, and the deck's declared noncreature-answer group is one card (Feed the Swarm) at 17.1%. Re-curating that group to name the two or three real answers would give the question a measured rate to argue against instead of a count.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Gate covers the missing class and takes the answer count from one to two; a third answer is diversification and needs a third priced cut on a deck at target on every other countable axis. Without a re-curated group there is no measured rate to price that trade.

gaps: The captain's log is EMPTY — `deck-notes yawgmoth-swarm list` returns no entries and there is no log_annotations.json. Nothing in this diagnosis rests on a played game; every behavioural claim is goldfish or simulation.

The one simulation run (giada-angels-vs-vito-vs-baylen-tokens-n20-5863d86b-s1482938475, 20 games) reports a 0.1 win rate with ci95 [0.028, 0.301]. That figure is NOT read as a measurement of this deck: the run's own assumptions block quotes Forge's docs saying the AI is 'pretty bad for most combo decks', and this deck's archetype is combo. Only the clock figures (round 17.1, elimination at global turn 30.44) and the elimination attribution are used, and even those come from an AI piloting our seat.

The 44.15 mean combat damage taken (ci95 [26.34, 61.96]) against giada-angels' 13.65 taken (ci95 [8.4, 18.9]) looks like a real separation on the marginals, but no interval on the DIFFERENCE was computed and the marginals alone do not license a comparison. It is recorded, not concluded from.

mana_analysis credits Pawn of Ulamog as a black source through land_colors' colour-identity fallback, although its only mana clause is the Eldrazi Spawn token's 'Sacrifice this token: Add {C}'. That is the same defect class the reminder-text fix just closed, differing only in that the granted ability sits in quotation marks rather than parentheses. The audit's figure of 2 is carried unchanged here; the bench should decide whether the fallback needs the same treatment.

deck_recon.json is as_of 2026-08-03, twenty-four days old, and predates the staples pass. Its fodder finding (Ophiomancer, Pawn of Ulamog) and its drain-redundancy finding (Marauding Blight-Priest, The Meathook Massacre) are already satisfied by the current 99. It is leaned on only for the mono-black mana finding, the Feed the Swarm finding and the failure modes.

No candidate_pool.json exists for this deck; Gate to Phyrexia and Culling the Weak were verified directly against data/cards.csv rather than drawn from a scored pool. A pool run scoped to artifact answers and to sacrifice-for-black-mana effects might name better candidates.

bracket_report.json carries no decklist_sha256, so the audit's freshness block reports current: null for it. The floor of 4 and both swap deltas were recomputed from the current 99 with bracket.assess and all return 4.

Supernatural Stamina and Plumb the Forbidden have no entry in card_roles.json, and Malakir Rebirth is filed ramp:ritual. All three carry engine-relevant functions no axis can count, which is why protection and card-advantage are read as floors rather than as verdicts.

The audit computes closers only for one-card components, so the tutor and engine-mana classes (both 61.2%) have no pool route in any artifact; they are named as the next-thinnest classes rather than prescribed for.
